chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:
The gambling (qimar) and the plundering (nuhba) are not valid.

key_terms.النُّهْبَةُ: Plundering or drawing lots; a game where items are placed in a bag and drawn by lot, or a form of gambling involving chance.
key_terms.الْمُقَامَرَةُ: Gambling; specifically refers to games played with dice or similar tools for winning a prize.
key_terms.تَصْلُحُ: Valid or permissible; in this context, it indicates the lack of validity or prohibition.

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Muqamarah and Nuhba in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi establishes the impermissibility of 'al-muqamarah' (gambling) and 'al-nuhba' (plundering via lots), serving as a foundational legal ruling in Shia jurisprudence regarding uncertain transactions. Scholarly tradition often links these specific terms to the broader prohibition of 'gharar' (uncertainty) and 'maysir' (games of chance), emphasizing their role in eroding social equity and wealth distribution. The ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on clarity and fairness in economic exchanges, distinguishing these practices from legitimate commercial activities.
